newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's computer imports rise 10 percent in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's computer imports rise 10 percent in 1995.

text.p: Tunisia's computer imports in 1995 rose 10 percent to 76.54 million dinars ($78.10 million), official statistics show.

The figures, published to coincide with an annual computer exhibition this week, showed that Tunisia imported 18,873 personal computers in 1995, up by 12.8 percent from 1994. Tunisia also imported 17,018 printers in 1995.
France was the leading source of Tunisia's computer imports in 1995 with nearly 30 percent of the total, followed by the United States with about 25 percent.
Computer imports totalled 69.56 million dinars in 1994. There are no customs duties on computer imports.
More than 70 foreign computer makers or dealers are represented in Tunisia, led by the IBM subsidiary Tunisian Business Machines TBM, official statistics show.

IBM announced last week it was making Tunis its headquarters for five North African countries (Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Tunisia and Mauritania) and Malta as part of its efforts to secure a larger share in the region's growing market.

Businessmen said 74 percent of Tunisia's computer imports went to the government, banks, insurance companies and big firms. Hotels and small firms accounted for 20 percent of the market and independent professions for the remaining six percent.
